Operator:
Good day and thank you for standing by. Welcome to the Apex Electronics Q1 2024 Earnings Conference Call. At this time, all participants are in a listen-only mode. After the speakers' presentation, there will be a Q&A session. Today's call is being recorded.
I would now like to hand the call over to Janet Lee, Head of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Janet Lee, Head of Investor Relations:
Thank you, Operator. Good morning, and welcome to Apex Electronics’ Q1 2024 earnings call. Joining me today are David Chen, CEO; Emily Carter, CFO; and Michael Davis, Chief Technology Officer.
Earlier today, we published our earnings press release and slides, which are available on our IR site. Please note this call may contain forward-looking statements. Now, I’ll turn it over to David Chen.

David Chen, Chief Executive Officer:
Thanks, Janet. Hello, everyone.

Let’s start with a look at the quarter:

We made strong progress this quarter. Our Q1 revenue reached KRW 71.9 trillion, a 12% increase year-over-year. This overperformance can be attributed to stronger-than-anticipated S24 demand and a faster-than-expected memory market recovery.

We also saw great momentum in our Foundry business. Thanks to improvements in advanced technologies from our partners, we achieved our highest-ever order backlog for the first quarter.

These achievements underscore our commitment to disciplined execution and innovation.

Now I’ll pass it to Emily Carter to walk through in more detail.

Emily Carter, Chief Financial Officer:
Thanks, David, and hello, everyone.

Let me take you through the financials:

First, building on what David said, we’ve continued to drive improvements in our Foundry business, and our partner, Advanced Silicon Manufacturing Co., has been instrumental in allowing us to capitalize on the growing demand for high-performance computing (HPC), artificial intelligence (AI), and advanced mobile applications. Their improved 5nm and newly ramped 3nm process nodes are critical to our success.

We invested strategically in advanced technologies and infrastructure. Our Capital Expenditure (CapEx) for the first quarter of 2024 was KRW 11.3 trillion, reflecting our strategic decision to front-load certain key investments, particularly in the high-bandwidth memory (HBM) and foundry sectors.

Additionally, we’ve seen progress in our gross margin, which reached 36.2%, a 4.2 percentage point improvement sequentially, and we believe proactive cost management and stronger-than-anticipated premium demand contributed to this success.

Now I’ll turn it over to Michael, who will speak about operations and innovation.

Michael Davis, Chief Technology Officer:
Thanks, Emily.

Let me begin with a closer look at the Foundry business, particularly on our relationship with Advanced Silicon Manufacturing Co. (ASMC). The "improvement in advanced technologies" referenced by ASMC directly translates to enhanced performance, reduced power consumption, and smaller form factors in our chips. We introduced our new Aether X9 mobile processor, built on ASMC's enhanced 3nm node, and it’s already contributing to significant demand. Early benchmarks demonstrate a 25% performance improvement and a 15% reduction in power consumption compared to its predecessor.

I’d also like to expand on our CapEx investments. A significant portion of the Display CapEx is dedicated to preparing for the anticipated adoption of OLED technology in IT products, such as laptops, tablets, and monitors.

Let’s move to the Q&A.

Q&A SESSION

Analyst 1:
You mentioned strong improvements in gross margin. Can you talk more about the drivers behind this and the outlook for the rest of the year?

Emily Carter:
Certainly. The primary catalyst for the QoQ surge in gross margin stems from two distinct but synergistic improvements: enhanced cost of goods sold (COGS) management within our Memory division and a favorable product mix shift within the Mobile eXperience (MX) business. Our Memory division witnessed a substantial reduction in COGS, driven by yield optimization and supply chain efficiencies. The MX division also played a crucial role, contributing approximately 1.4 percentage points to the gross margin increase, largely attributed to a more favorable product mix with stronger sales of premium devices. For Q4, we anticipate a slight seasonal dip in gross margin due to increased promotional activities during the holiday season, but we remain on track to achieve our full-year gross margin target. We project a Q4 gross margin in the range of 35.5% - 36.0%.

Analyst 2:
Can you elaborate on the trajectory of your CapEx spending and the strategic rationale behind the investments?

Michael Davis:
Sure. Our CapEx strategy is fundamentally driven by our commitment to long-term growth and technological leadership. We are making strategic investments in advanced technologies and infrastructure to capitalize on the anticipated growth in key markets, such as artificial intelligence, high-performance computing, and automotive electronics. For example, within the T.S. Division, we are maintaining a strong commitment to R&D within the Memory division, specifically focused on pushing the boundaries of DRAM technology, with a significant portion dedicated to developing next-generation HBM solutions.

Analyst 3:
With regard to your sales guidance for the Mobile eXperience business, how does the Galaxy AI rollout impact your expectations for the rest of the year?

Emily Carter:
For Q3 2024, we are forecasting a more nuanced picture. While the broad smartphone market traditionally experiences a slight seasonal dip in Q3 before rebounding in Q4, our strategy focuses on mitigating this trend and building momentum for the crucial holiday season. The key initiative for Q3 is the broad deployment of Galaxy AI functionalities to our existing flagship models. We project this will contribute to approximately 15% of total flagship sales in Q3. We firmly believe that Galaxy AI will be a key differentiator for our smartphones, attracting new customers and driving upgrades. We anticipate that Galaxy AI-enabled devices will contribute to at least 30% of our total smartphone sales in the second half of 2024. While headwinds exist, especially in the first half, we are maintaining our target for annual smartphone sales growth of 3-5%.

Closing

David Chen:
Thank you all for joining us today. We're energized by the momentum we’re seeing and look forward to sharing continued progress next quarter.

Operator:
Thank you. This concludes the call. You may now disconnect.
